text:
Maya R: Heads-up — I'm sketching a small panel to track prefix cache reuse by route and kernel selection impact. Need quick input on what to show.
Samir: Love it. High level: hit rate, evictions/sec, mem-bytes, reuse_ratio (route hits / route requests) per 1m. Also show dominant kernel chosen during requests.
Kevin L: From profiling yesterday, kernel choice correlates with seq_len distribution — when kernel B is selected we see 2x cache churn for long prefixes. I can post the trace.
Alyssa: For the dashboard queries, I'd propose PromQL and a ClickHouse fallback. Example PromQL for reuse_ratio: ```sum by(route) (rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum by(route) (rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))```
Jia: Also add a metric for "reuse_after_eviction" — fraction of requests that hit a warm KV after an eviction within Xs. That helps detect thrashing.
Maya R: Good call. For kernel selection add a stacked bar showing percent of requests served by kernel_x where x in {A,B,C}. Can we tag requests with selected_kernel in traces?
Kevin L: Yes, we have a trace attribute `runtime.kernel` already. Perf note: attached pprof snippet showed KV cache lookups taking 18% of CPU during the spike; root cause appears to be repeated small batches causing more KV hash churn.
```
perf: samples: 1000
  180  runtime.kv.lookup
  120  runtime.kernel.select
  80   runtime.batch.dispatch
```
Samir: That pprof pattern implies batching heuristics matter. If small batches (1-4) dominate, we get more cache index ops per token. Suggest panel with tokens_per_request percentile and batch_size distribution.
Alyssa: For memory footprint: ClickHouse query I drafted: ```SELECT route, sum(bytes) as mem FROM kv_cache_items GROUP BY route ORDER BY mem DESC LIMIT 50``` — we can surface top routes by memory.
perf-bot: :warning: Alert: kv_cache_evictions_total spike detected on 2024-11-02T14:18:05Z — +1200 evictions in 5m for region=us-west-2.
Maya R: That alert correlates with a rollout where kernel B was enabled for canary routes. Jia, can you correlate evictions->kernel timeline?
Jia: On it. Initial look: when kernel B ramps to ~20% for /chat-route-2 we see evictions up 3x. Hypothesis: kernel B creates different prefix keys (ordering of kv segments) leading to less reuse across concurrent requests.
Kevin L: Also saw increased tail latency on token-level breakdown: token.gen.rpc_queue + token.gen.kv_lookup accounted for 45% of 95p latency during the window.
Alyssa: Proposed dashboard tabs: Overview (hit rate, mem, evictions), Per-route (reuse_ratio, mem_per_request), Kernel impact (kernel share, per-kernel hitrate), Batching (batch_size distribution, tokens/request).
Samir: For alerts: fire when per-route reuse_ratio falls below 0.6 and evictions/sec > 50 for >5m. Also alert when batch_size_p50 < 3 and tokens_per_request_p50 > 40 simultaneously (indicates inefficient batching on long requests).
Maya R: I'll create the Grafana panel draft and add an "investigate" drilldown that opens the relevant traces and pprof snapshots. Will also add a short note on mitigation: fallback to kernel A for routes with reuse_ratio < 0.5 until cache warms.
Jia: FYI, I'll instrument a new metric `kv_prefix_key_variants{route}` counting distinct prefix key shapes per 1m; should help confirm the kernel-keying hypothesis.
Kevin L: If Jia adds that, we can add a heatmap: variants vs hit_rate.
perf-bot: :white_check_mark: Metric kv_prefix_key_variants registered in prod metric-store.
Maya R: Thanks all — let's review the draft tomorrow 11:00am PT. Action items: Alyssa (queries + panel skeleton), Jia (variants metric + correlation job), Kevin (upload pprof + trace links), Samir (alert rules).
